name: slice
title: Slice the likelihood of a clm

origin.description: Slice likelihood and plot the slice. This is usefull for illustrating the likelihood surface around the MLE (maximum likelihood estimate) and provides graphics to substantiate (non-)convergence of a model fit. Also, the closeness of a quadratic approximation to the log-likelihood function can be inspected for relevant parameters. A slice is considerably less computationally demanding than a profile.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: for the clm method an object of class "clm", i.e., the result of a call to clm.

arguments.name: parm
arguments.text: a numeric or character vector indexing parameters. By default all parameters are selected.

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.text: the number of curvature units on each side of the MLE the slice should cover.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.text: the number of values at which to compute the log-likelihood for each parameter.

arguments.name: quad.approx
arguments.text: compute and include the quadratic approximation to the log-likelihood function?

origin.details: The clm method evaluates the relative log-likelihood along a grid in each requested parameter, optionally adding a quadratic approximation from the Hessian curvature.
origin.value: A list of data.frames with parameter values, relative logLik, and optional quad column. The original fit is stored as attribute original.fit.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ordinal))
data(wine)
fm1 <- clm(rating ~ contact + temp, data = wine)
sl1 <- slice(fm1, parm = 1, grid = 10)
print(sl1[[1]])

translation.description: Slice likelihood and plot the slice. This is usefull for illustrating the likelihood surface around the MLE (maximum likelihood estimate) and provides graphics to substantiate (non-)convergence of a model fit. Also, the closeness of a quadratic approximation to the log-likelihood function can be inspected for relevant parameters. A slice is considerably less computationally demanding than a profile.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: a fitted cumulative link model carrying coefficients, logLik, Hessian, and an internal rho environment (ClmLike today; clm when that fitter is translated).

arguments.name: parm
arguments.text: integer indices or coefficient names selecting parameters to slice.

arguments.name: lambda_
arguments.text: curvature units on each side of the MLE.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.text: number of grid points per parameter.

arguments.name: quad_approx
arguments.text: include the quadratic log-likelihood approximation column.

translation.details: The clm method evaluates the relative log-likelihood along a grid in each requested parameter, optionally adding a quadratic approximation from the Hessian curvature.
translation.value: A SliceClm list-like object with one dict per parameter (parameter values, logLik, optional quad). The original fit is stored on original_fit.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from ordinal._clm_rho import clm_like_from_npz
from ordinal.slice import slice_clm

obj = clm_like_from_npz("proof/slice_wine_rho.npz")
sl1 = slice_clm(obj, parm=1, grid=10, quad_approx=True)
frame = sl1[0]
name = next(iter(frame))
print(np.column_stack([frame[name], frame["logLik"], frame["quad"]]))
